rv.q: With a sizzling, gut-wrenching performance from Christine Ebersole as the fraught and ill-used central character in Jeff Calhoun's production, this moving, exquisitely performed show should be the prestige Broadway attraction of the fall.
In a Broadway arena that can be unaccommodating for “serious” musicals, “Grey Gardens” is as boldly odd, original and beguiling as its subjects.
"Grey Gardens," the musical about the bizarre cousin and aunt of Jacqueline Bouvier Kennedy Onassis, has taken over the Theatre as if to the manor born.
And when Ms. Ebersole, portraying the middle-aged, time-warped debutante called Little Edie Beale, delivers her das and dums, any doubts that this show belongs on Broadway are sent packing.
The musical succeeds because it respects its source material without condescending to it.
York is so dominant in the role, gracefully balancing hilarity with pathos
Ebersole already has a Tony, but this performance catapults her high into the Broadway heavens.
This is a musical that works on every level - as entertainment, as a portrait of faded gentility, and as a showcase for two magnificent performances.
They are compelling, hysterically funny, yet gut wrenchingly sad, capturing the bizarre spirit of this unique relationship.
But it has become so at the expense of Ebersole's luminescence and the electric theatricality it generated.
